core_obligations: Reduce the statement to the linear independence of the images of f_1 to f_m in the cotangent space (proof lines 11826-11830).

Suppose a nontrivial linear relation among those images, so that a combination of the f_i lies in the square of the maximal ideal with coefficients not all in the maximal ideal (proof lines 11830-11834).

Apply each derivation to the combination, use the Leibniz rule and the containment of the square of the maximal ideal in the maximal ideal, and obtain a vanishing linear combination of the rows of the derivative matrix (proof lines 11834-11840).
Conclude that the determinant cannot be a unit, which is the contradiction, and deduce both claimed consequences (proof lines 11840-11841).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to linear independence in the cotangent space (proof lines 11826-11830).
Assume a relation and control its coefficients (proof lines 11830-11834).
Apply the derivations and contradict invertibility of the determinant (proof lines 11834-11841).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a Jacobian criterion for a sequence of elements of the maximal ideal of a regular local ring to be a regular sequence cutting out a regular quotient, and the proof is a 16-line argument in two steps. It first reduces the statement to the linear independence of the residues of the elements in the cotangent space, then argues by contradiction: a nontrivial linear relation with coefficients that are not all in the maximal ideal would, after applying the derivations and using the Leibniz rule together with the fact that the derivations carry the square of the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal, produce a vanishing linear combination of the determinant rows, contradicting the invertibility of the determinant. Both the reduction and the contradiction computation are displayed.
